land.text: the satrapy of Bactria: the kingdom 'was founded by the Seleucid satrap Diodotus I Soter in about 256 BC'

predecessors.note: The page also gives 255 BC (high chronology), 246 BC (low) and 'around 250 BC'; the seleucid-empire dossier dates the secession to 245 from another page.

land.text: Bactria, which the Yuezhi invaded 'from 130 BC' and held to c. 120 (Heliocles page)

successors.note: Cliopatria's Yuezhi row takes Bactria in 126.

land.text: the land south of the Hindu Kush: Heliocles 'abandoned Bactria and moved his capital to the Kabul valley'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Indo-Greeks row starts in 126 with 2,835 of the 2,841 cells the Greco-Bactrian shape already holds for 144-127.

capitals.name: Bactra (Balkh)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Bactra (Balkh), with Ai-Khanoum listed as a city. Antiochus III besieged Euthydemus there for three years (208-206).

capitals.name: Ai-Khanoum
capitals.note: 'Eucratides was the last known ruler of Ai-Khanoum, which was also his capital city.' Dates of its use as capital are the researcher's reading from his reign (171-145) and Heliocles in Eastern Bactria.

capitals.name: Kabul valley
capitals.note: Heliocles 'abandoned Bactria and moved his capital to the Kabul valley', undated on the page; no city is named and Kabul is the valley's modern seat.

correction.text: the satrapy of Bactria with Margiana and part of Sogdia, as in the first Cliopatria shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -256..-248: Cliopatria's row begins in 247 but the page says the kingdom 'was founded by the Seleucid satrap Diodotus I Soter in about 256 BC' (infobox 'Established: 256 BC'; 255 or 246 in the high and low chronologies). The 247 shape (Bactria, Margiana and the southern Sogdia, 422,343 km2 at its resolved size) is used for the earlier years; the page gives no boundary.
488,619 km2 on 60.3-72.4 E, 34.4-41.1 N: Bactria, Margiana and part of Sogdia. The page gives its 2,500,000 km2 only for 184 BC, so no ratio is possible for the early years.

488,960 km2. Cliopatria's bounding box starts at 29.4 E, a stray fragment far to the west; the resolved shape (checked for 230) spans 60.3-72.3 E. Diodotus II succeeds Diodotus I and 'allied with the Parthian Arsaces against Seleucus II' (page); no border change.

489,263 km2, the same area. Euthydemus I 'usurped power from Diodotus II in 224 BC' (page; the main page says 'around 230-220 BC'). Antiochus III's attack and the three-year siege of Bactra (208-206) leave the shape unchanged.

685,135 km2 for -203..-171, against the infobox's 2,500,000 km2 for 184 BC: ratio 0.27, well beyond a factor of two. The shape adds the Sogdia/Fergana strip (166k km2, 64-74 E, 37.6-42.4 N) in 203, which fits 'Euthydemus expanded the Bactrian territory into Sogdia' (Euthydemus page) but omits Demetrius I's conquest of 'the Kabul valley, Sindh and a part of Punjab' that began 'between 190 and 180 BC' and was 'completed by 175'. The shape is right for -203..-181; keyframe -180 carries -180..-171. Even with the Indian cells the area is 0.98 M km2, so the infobox figure also counts claims such as Strabo's reach to the Seres and is read as a maximum.

correction.text: the 203 shape plus the Kabul valley, Gandhara, the Punjab and Sindh

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -180..-171: the 203 shape plus Demetrius I's Indian conquests, 'conquered extensive areas in what is now southern Afghanistan, Pakistan and northwestern India'; a note says he 'annexed the Kabul valley, Sindh and a part of Punjab'. Gandhara is added because Demetrius 'is generally considered' to have ruled at Taxila (Sirkap). The page does not mention Drangiana; Arachosia only as 'may have first started to recover'. Pakistan's Punjab stands for 'a part of Punjab'.

1,364,110 km2 (ratio 0.55 to the infobox's 2.5 M for 184 BC): the shape grows by 625k km2 (2,472 cells, 66.5-79.3 E, 27.8-42.2 N, including the Kabul valley, Gandhara and most of the Punjab) in 170, the year after Eucratides' coup (c. 171). The page: Eucratides 'conquered parts of India, campaigning as far south as Barigaza' and 'successfully fought against the Indo-Greek kings'; it dates neither. The shape still holds Margiana (294 cells), which the same page has the Parthians taking from 'Demetrius ... in about 170 BC'.

1,194,248 km2: Margiana and Aria are gone from the shape in 164 (740 cells lost, west and east). The page gives two dates, 'about 170 BC' for Mithridates I taking Tapuria and Margiana from Demetrius, and 'From 162-158 BCE, Eucratides lost the satrapies of Aria and Margiana'; the shape sits between them. The ledger uses 158 for the completed loss. The main page says instead that Mithridates gained 'Bactria's territory west of the Arius, the regions of Tapuria and Traxiane'.

1,099,129 km2 for -144..-127: 2,835 cells of it are the same as Cliopatria's Indo-Greeks shape for 126, and the rest is Bactria (1,071 cells). It drops 321 cells in 144 (246 of them into Cliopatria's Yuezhi shape: Sogdia and Fergana). The Heliocles page has him in 'Eastern Bactria' (145-130) and 'From 130 BC a nomadic people, the Yuezhi, started to invade Bactria', so the shape stands for -144..-131 only; -130..-127 take keyframe -130.

correction.text: the 144 shape without Bactria: the Kabul valley and the Indian conquests

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -130..-127: the Yuezhi take Bactria ('From 130 BC ... started to invade Bactria from the north'; the table lists 'Yuezhi occupation' of Bactria 130-120); the main page has Heliocles abandoning Bactria for the Kabul valley. What is left is the south-of-the-Hindu-Kush part of the 144 shape, which becomes the Indo-Greeks in Cliopatria's rows from 126. The Zhang Qian visit of 126 (main page) finds Bactria's 'political system gone'.

ledger.note: 256 BC: Diodotus I Soter, the Seleucid satrap, founds the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom in Bactria. The page: 'was founded by the Seleucid satrap Diodotus I Soter in about 256 BC'; infobox 'Established: 256 BC'; also 255 BC (high chronology), 246 BC (low) and 'around 250 BC'. The page names the satrapy by its name, not a boundary.

224 BC: Euthydemus I overthrows Diodotus II and starts a new dynasty. 'He is thought to have originally been a satrap of Sogdia, who usurped power from Diodotus II in 224 BC' (the main page: 'around 230-220 BC'). Same state; colour continues.

208 BC: Antiochus III attacks Bactria. 'Little is known of his reign until 208 BC when he was attacked by Antiochus III the Great' (lead: 209 to 206); Euthydemus 'tried in vain to resist on the shores of the river Arius' and then 'successfully resisted a three-year siege in the fortified city of Bactra'. The main page dates the attack 'around 210 BC'.
206 BC: peace. Antiochus agreed to recognise Euthydemus's rule and 'to offer one of his daughters to Euthydemus's son Demetrius around 206 BC', and was given war elephants.

region.text: 166k km2 of Sogdia and Ferghana added by the 203 shape

ledger.note: 203: the kingdom grows north into Sogdia and Ferghana. 'Euthydemus expanded the Bactrian territory into Sogdia' (Euthydemus page) and 'To the north, Euthydemus also ruled Sogdiana and Ferghana' (main page). Neither page dates it (his reign is 224-195); 203 is Cliopatria's shape change, and the page does not say who held Sogdia before (Euthydemus is thought to have been satrap of Sogdia).

region.text: the Kabul valley, Gandhara and the Punjab

ledger.note: c. 190 BC: Demetrius I invades north-west India. 'Demetrius started the invasion of northwestern India between 190 and 180 BC', after 'the destruction of the Mauryan dynasty by the general Pushyamitra Shunga'. The earliest year of the page's range.

region.text: the Kabul valley, Gandhara, the Punjab and Sindh

ledger.note: c. 180 BC: Demetrius I annexes the Kabul valley, Sindh and part of the Punjab. 'He annexed the Kabul valley, Sindh and a part of Punjab' (note); the invasion began 'before 180 BC'. The main page says it 'was completed by 175 BC, creating the Indo-Greek Kingdom'. The land is read as Mauryan remnant (Shunga held the Gangetic plain). Reviewer me-05-e: counterpart set to nobody (was maurya-empire): the main page dates the invasion 'a few years after the Mauryan empire had been overthrown by the Shunga dynasty', and the maurya-empire dossier ends in 185 with the north-west lost to nobody from 225.

region.text: the Kabul valley, Gandhara, the Punjab and Sindh

ledger.note: 175 BC: the conquest is complete. 'was completed by 175 BC'; by then the Indo-Greeks ruled parts of north-west India while the Shungas held the Gangetic, central and eastern regions (Demetrius page).

c. 171 BC: Eucratides seizes power in Bactria. 'seems to have seized power through a coup around 171 BC'; infobox reign 171-145; the Eucratides page names Antimachus I as the probable king he dethroned. The Euthydemid line ends; same state.

region.text: the Indian land the 170 shape adds beyond the Kabul valley, Gandhara, Punjab and Sindh of 180

ledger.note: 170: the Indian holdings grow. The 170 shape is 625k km2 larger than the 203 shape, 373k of it beyond the Kabul valley, Gandhara, Punjab and Sindh already given at 180. The Eucratides page: he 'conquered parts of India, campaigning as far south as Barigaza' and 'successfully fought against the Indo-Greek kings', undated; the year and cells are Cliopatria's. Land the Indo-Greek kings held is the counterpart.
c. 170 BC: Mithridates I of Parthia takes Margiana. 'Having taken Tapuria and Margiana from Demetrius in about 170 BC, Mithridates I attempted to conquer Bactria but was checked by Eucratides.'

region.text: the satrapies of Aria and Margiana

ledger.note: 158 BC: Aria and Margiana are lost to the Parthians. 'From 162-158 BCE, Eucratides lost the satrapies of Aria and Margiana to Mithridates I of Parthia.' The main page instead has Mithridates gaining 'Bactria's territory west of the Arius, the regions of Tapuria and Traxiane'.
158 BC: the fighting with Parthia ends at the end of the page's 162-158 span.

region.text: the northern cells (Sogdia and Fergana) the 144 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 144: Sogdia and Fergana pass to the Yuezhi. Cliopatria's shape drops 321 cells, 246 of them into its Yuezhi shape (66.9-73.3 E, 40.2-42.2 N). The page: Eucratides 'was killed by his own son in about 145 BC, which may have further destabilised the kingdom' and 'Around 140 BC, eastern Scythians (the Saka) started to invade various parts of Parthia and Bactria'. No page opened dates the loss of Sogdia.

130 BC: the Yuezhi invade Bactria. 'From 130 BC a nomadic people, the Yuezhi, started to invade Bactria from the north'; the table lists 'Yuezhi occupation' of Bactria 130-120; the main page: 'The Yuezhi further expanded southward into Bactria around 120 BC'. Cliopatria's Yuezhi row takes Bactria in 126.

130 BC: Heliocles leaves Bactria for the Kabul valley. 'Heliocles was the last Greek king to rule in Bactria' and 'abandoned Bactria and moved his capital to the Kabul valley'; the page gives no year, so the year of the Yuezhi invasion is used.

region.text: what remained south of the Hindu Kush

ledger.note: 127 BC: the Greek kingdom of Bactria is over. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 120 BC'; the Heliocles page has his reign to 130 (table) or 120, and Zhang Qian, who 'actually visited Bactria (named Daxia in Chinese) in 126 BC', found its political system gone. 127 is Cliopatria's last year and the year before the Indo-Greeks row begins; the land south of the Hindu Kush continues as the Indo-Greek Kingdom.

wars.name: Siege of Bactra (Antiochus III's campaign)
wars.outcome: Euthydemus lost the battle on the Arius, then resisted a three-year siege of Bactra; Antiochus recognised his rule and promised a daughter to Demetrius (c. 206).

wars.name: Demetrius I's invasion of India

zones.text: the Kabul valley, Gandhara and the Punjab

wars.outcome: Demetrius annexed the Kabul valley, Sindh and part of the Punjab; 'completed by 175 BC' on the main page, which names the result the Indo-Greek Kingdom.
wars.note: The page says the Greek campaigns 'may have gone as far as the capital Pataliputra' but attributes that to Menander I; the Shungas kept the Gangetic plain.

wars.name: Eucratides' wars with the Indo-Greek kings
wars.outcome: Eucratides 'conquered parts of India' as far as Barigaza and was 'besieged by Demetrius, king of the Indians', whom the page identifies uncertainly (Demetrius I, Demetrius II or Menander I); killed returning from India c. 145.
wars.note: No year for the siege or the conquests; the ledger's 170 gain is the Cliopatria shape change.

wars.name: Parthian conquest of Aria and Margiana

zones.text: Aria and Margiana (Tapuria and Traxiane on the main page)

wars.outcome: Mithridates I took Margiana (about 170), then 'From 162-158 BCE' Aria and Margiana, but was 'checked by Eucratides' in Bactria; the main page adds an alliance with the Seleucid Demetrius II against Parthia in 141.

wars.name: Yuezhi and Saka invasions of Bactria
wars.outcome: Heliocles, 'considered the last Greek king to reign over the Bactrian country', lost Bactria to the Yuezhi; Zhang Qian found it in 126 without a political system.
wars.note: The main page puts the Saka invasions around 140 and the Yuezhi into Bactria 'around 120 BC'; the Heliocles page has the Yuezhi invading from 130.

certainty.note: Satrapy and city frontiers (Bactra, Ai-Khanoum, Taxila, the Arius), the Oxus, the Hindu Kush and the Indus plain are approximate; no treaty fixed a line, and the Indian conquests have only a footnote's regions.

sources.title: Heliocles I
sources.note: Last Greek king in Bactria; Yuezhi from 130; no capital move on this page.

notes: Cliopatria's row is the Greco-Bactrians and the Indo-Greeks run together: the 144..127 shape is Bactria plus 2,835 cells identical to the Indo-Greeks' 126 shape, and the 170..164 shapes carry Demetrius's and Eucratides' Indian conquests. The indo-greeks dossier (another group) should take the Indian land from 180 or 170 and this dossier's cells should then not be drawn twice; the pages opened do not separate the two kingdoms by year (Demetrius I is on the Demetrius page a Greco-Bactrian reign c. 200-180 and an Indo-Greek reign to 180 or 167). Dates disagree across pages: foundation 256 (infobox), 255, 250, 246; the seleucid-empire dossier has the secession in 245 from its own page. The end is the weakest date: infobox c. 120 BC, Heliocles page reign to 130 (table) or 120, Yuezhi invasion from 130 or around 120, Zhang Qian's 126 visit; -127 is Cliopatria's last year and is kept as the dissolve (confidence 1) with Bactria itself given to the Yuezhi in 130 (confidence 2); the yuezhi dossier (ia-01) should mirror 130 or explain Cliopatria's 126. Not on the pages: Diodotus's Sogdian and Parthian dealings, Euthydemus II, Pantaleon, Agathocles, Antimachus, Apollodotus, Menander (kings' table only), the Seres/Phryni claim (Strabo, quoted without territory), the identity of 'Demetrius, king of the Indians', Taxila and Sirkap as capitals (not on the main page), Traxiane and Tapuria locations (no gazetteer regions). The rulers strip is omitted: the table has Diodotus I 255-239, Diodotus II 239-223, Euthydemus I 230-200 (224-195 on his page), Demetrius I 200-180, Eucratides 171-145, Heliocles 140-130, with undated kings between 180 and 171 and contradictory overlaps. Sogdia/Fergana (203) are added with the counterpart 'nobody' because the page does not name the previous holder. Gazetteer: all region names resolve ('Bactria', 'Margiana', 'Aria', 'Kabulistan', 'Gandhara', Punjab and Sind of Pakistan); Tapuria and Traxiane would be new names if a later agent needs them. Page budget: 5 pages.
